words.gloss: the sum of the constituent elements

hindi: राजा और राज्य — यह प्रकृतियों का संक्षेप है।
english: The king and the kingdom: this is the sum of the constituent elements.
notes: saṅkṣepa = abridgement: the seven prakṛtis are summed up as king (svāmin) and kingdom (the other six).
lines_deva: राजा राज्यम् इति प्रकृति.सङ्क्षेपः

hindi: राजा का कोप आन्तरिक अथवा बाह्य होता है — यह विषय है।
english: A revolt (kopa) against the king is either internal or external: this is the topic.
notes: kopa literally 'anger'; here the disaffection or revolt that is a calamity of the king (the genitive rājñaḥ is literally 'of the king'). iti marks the line as a heading of the topic discussed next.
lines_deva: राज्ञो ऽभ्यन्तरो बाह्यो वा कोप इति

words.gloss: than / like the fear of a snake

hindi: सर्प के भय के समान आन्तरिक कोप बाह्य कोप से अधिक अनिष्टकारी है, और भीतरी अमात्यों का कोप आन्तरिक कोप से भी अधिक अनिष्टकारी है।
english: Like the danger from a snake, internal revolt is worse than external revolt; and revolt of the ministers within is worse than internal revolt.
notes: ahi-bhayāt is an ablative of comparison read here as a simile ('as with fear of a snake [close at hand]'); it could also be causal ('because of a snake-like danger'). The second clause supplies pāpīyān from the first.
lines_deva: अहि.भयाद् अभ्यन्तरः कोपो बाह्य.कोपात् पापीयान्, अन्तर्.अमात्य.कोपश् च-अन्तः.कोपात्
lines_iast: ahi.bhayād abhyantaraḥ kopo bāhya.kopāt pāpīyān, antar.amātya.kopaś ca-antaḥ.kopāt

words.gloss: the power of treasury and army

hindi: इसलिए कोश और दण्ड की शक्ति को अपने ही अधीन रखे।
english: Therefore he should keep the power of treasury and army under his own control.
lines_deva: तस्मात् कोश.दण्ड.शक्तिम् आत्म.संस्थां कुर्वीत

words.gloss: of dual rule and foreign rule
by hatred and partiality towards each other's party
looking to winning the hearts of the constituent elements

hindi: "द्वैराज्य और वैराज्य में से द्वैराज्य एक-दूसरे के पक्ष के प्रति द्वेष और अनुराग से अथवा परस्पर संघर्ष से नष्ट हो जाता है; वैराज्य तो प्रकृतियों के चित्त को जीतने की अपेक्षा रखता हुआ, जैसा है वैसा ही दूसरों के द्वारा भोगा जाता है" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: "Of dual rule (dvairājya) and foreign rule (vairājya), dual rule perishes through hatred and partiality towards each other's party, or through mutual rivalry; foreign rule, however, looking to the winning of the hearts of the constituent elements, is enjoyed by others as it stands," say the teachers.
notes: dvairājya = rule by two kings jointly; vairājya = rule by a foreigner (one who is not the hereditary king). anyaiḥ 'by others' = the foreign rulers.
lines_deva: "द्वैराज्य.वैराज्ययोर् द्वैराज्यम् अन्योन्य.पक्ष.द्वेष.अनुरागाभ्यां परस्पर.सङ्घर्षेण वा विनश्यति, वैराज्यं तु प्रकृति.चित्त.ग्रहण.अपेक्षि यथा.स्थितम् अन्यैर् भुज्यते" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: "dvairājya.vairājyayor dvairājyam anyonya.pakṣa.dveṣa.anurāgābhyāṃ paraspara.saṅgharṣeṇa vā vinaśyati, vairājyaṃ tu prakṛti.citta.grahaṇa.apekṣi yathā.sthitam anyair bhujyate" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: नहीं, ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: "No," says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः

hindi: पिता-पुत्र का अथवा दो भाइयों का द्वैराज्य, जिसमें योग और क्षेम समान हों और अमात्यों का नियन्त्रण हो, चलता रहता है।
english: Dual rule of father and son or of two brothers, with equal acquisition and security and with restraint by the ministers, carries on.
notes: tulya-yoga-kṣemam and amātya-avagraham taken as adjectives of dvairājyam; they could also be adverbial accusatives ('carries on with equal yoga-kṣema and under ministers' restraint'). amātya-avagraha = the check that ministers exercise (alternatively 'a hold over the ministers').
lines_deva: पिता.पुत्रयोर् भ्रात्रोर् वा द्वैराज्यं तुल्य.योग.क्षेमम् अमात्य.अवग्रहं वर्तयति
lines_iast: pitā.putrayor bhrātror vā dvairājyaṃ tulya.yoga.kṣemam amātya.avagrahaṃ vartayati

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. ātm. √man

hindi: वैराज्य में तो, जीवित दूसरे से राज्य छीनकर "यह मेरा नहीं है" ऐसा मानता हुआ वह उसे क्षीण करता है, उसका धन ले जाता है, अथवा उसे बिक्री की वस्तु बना देता है, अथवा उसके विरक्त हो जाने पर उसे छोड़कर चला जाता है।
english: Foreign rule, however: having wrested (the kingdom) from another who is alive, thinking "this is not mine", he impoverishes it, carries (its wealth) away, or makes it an article of sale, or, when it has become disaffected, abandons it and goes away.
notes: The object (the kingdom) is understood from vairājyam. apavāhayati 'causes to be carried off' = drains its wealth; viraktam 'disaffected' agrees with the understood kingdom (its people). Hindi 'धन' after apavāhayati is supplied (the Sanskrit has no object).
lines_deva: वैराज्यं तु जीवतः परस्य-आच्छिद्य "न-एतन् मम" इति मन्यमानः कर्शयति, अपवाहयति, पण्यं वा करोति, विरक्तं वा परित्यज्य-अपगच्छति-इति
lines_iast: vairājyaṃ tu jīvataḥ parasya-ācchidya "na-etan mama" iti manyamānaḥ karśayati, apavāhayati, paṇyaṃ vā karoti, viraktaṃ vā parityajya-apagacchati-iti

hindi: "अन्धा राजा अथवा शास्त्र से विचलित राजा" — इस विषय में "शास्त्ररूपी नेत्र से रहित अन्धा राजा, मन में जो आए वही करने वाला, हठी अथवा दूसरों के द्वारा चलाया जाने वाला होकर अन्याय से राज्य का नाश कर देता है; किन्तु शास्त्र से विचलित राजा जिस विषय में उसकी बुद्धि शास्त्र से हट जाती है, उसमें समझाया जा सकता है" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: "A blind king or one deviating from the science (śāstra)": "The blind one, lacking the eye of the science, doing whatever comes to him, firmly obstinate or led by others, destroys the kingdom by injustice; the one deviating from the science, however, in whatever matter his mind deviates from the science, there becomes amenable to persuasion," say the teachers.
notes: 'blind' = ignorant of the science of politics (aśāstra-cakṣuḥ), not literally sightless. The first rājā iti states the topic (which of the two is worse).
lines_deva: अन्धश् चलित.शास्त्रो वा राजा-इति "अशास्त्र.चक्षुर् अन्धो यत्.किञ्चन.कारी दृढ.अभिनिवेशी पर.प्रणेयो वा राज्यम् अन्यायेन-उपहन्ति, चलित.शास्त्रस् तु यत्र शास्त्राच् चलित.मतिर् भवति शक्य.अनुनयो भवति" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: andhaś calita.śāstro vā rājā-iti "aśāstra.cakṣur andho yat.kiñcana.kārī dṛḍha.abhiniveśī para.praṇeyo vā rājyam anyāyena-upahanti, calita.śāstras tu yatra śāstrāc calita.matir bhavati śakya.anunayo bhavati" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: नहीं, ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: "No," says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः

hindi: अन्धे राजा को सहायकों की सम्पत् के बल पर किसी भी विषय में ठीक मार्ग पर स्थापित किया जा सकता है।
english: A blind king can be set right in any matter whatever through the excellence of his helpers.
notes: yatra tatra vā 'in this matter or that' = in whatever matter arises.
lines_deva: अन्धो राजा शक्यते सहाय.सम्पदा यत्र तत्र वा पर्यवस्थापयितुम्
lines_iast: andho rājā śakyate sahāya.sampadā yatra tatra vā paryavasthāpayitum

hindi: किन्तु शास्त्र से विचलित राजा, जिसकी बुद्धि शास्त्र के विपरीत जमी हुई है, अन्याय से राज्य और अपने आप को नष्ट कर देता है।
english: But the one deviating from the science, his mind set otherwise than the science, destroys by injustice both the kingdom and himself.
lines_deva: चलित.शास्त्रस् तु शास्त्राद् अन्यथा.अभिनिविष्ट.बुद्धिर् अन्यायेन राज्यम् आत्मानं च-उपहन्ति-इति
lines_iast: calita.śāstras tu śāstrād anyathā.abhiniviṣṭa.buddhir anyāyena rājyam ātmānaṃ ca-upahanti-iti

words.gloss: by acts of favour, exemption, gift and honour belonging to his own dharma
by benefits that please the constituent elements

hindi: "रोगी राजा अथवा नया राजा" — इस विषय में "रोगी राजा अमात्यों के कारण होने वाली राज्य की हानि को अथवा राज्य के कारण होने वाली प्राणों की पीड़ा को प्राप्त होता है; नया राजा तो अपने धर्म के अनुसार अनुग्रह, परिहार, दान और मान के कर्मों से तथा प्रकृतियों को प्रसन्न करने वाले उपकारों से आचरण करता है" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: "A sick king or a new king": "A sick king incurs injury to the kingdom rooted in the ministers, or affliction of his life rooted in the kingdom; a new king, however, acts with acts of favour, exemption, gift and honour belonging to his own dharma, and with benefits that please the constituent elements," say the teachers.
notes: amātya-mūlam and rājya-mūlam taken as bahuvrīhi adjectives of upaghātam and ābādham. sva-dharma- could also be read as 'in keeping with (the subjects') own dharma'; parihāra = remission of taxes.
lines_deva: व्याधितो नवो वा राजा-इति "व्याधितो राजा राज्य.उपघातम् अमात्य.मूलं प्राण.आबाधं वा राज्य.मूलम् अवाप्नोति, नवस् तु राजा स्व.धर्म.अनुग्रह.परिहार.दान.मान.कर्मभिः प्रकृति.रञ्जन.उपकारैश् चरति" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: vyādhito navo vā rājā-iti "vyādhito rājā rājya.upaghātam amātya.mūlaṃ prāṇa.ābādhaṃ vā rājya.mūlam avāpnoti, navas tu rājā sva.dharma.anugraha.parihāra.dāna.māna.karmabhiḥ prakṛti.rañjana.upakāraiś carati" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: नहीं, ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: "No," says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः

words.gloss: as it has been going on

hindi: रोगी राजा राज-प्रशासन को जैसा चला आ रहा है वैसा ही चलाता रहता है।
english: A sick king keeps the royal administration going as it has been carried on.
notes: rāja-praṇidhi: the king's established arrangement / administration.
lines_deva: व्याधितो राजा यथा.प्रवृत्तं राज.प्रणिधिम् अनुवर्तयति

hindi: नया राजा तो बल से जीते हुए राज्य को "यह राज्य मेरा है" ऐसा मानकर निरंकुश होकर मनमाना आचरण करता है।
english: A new king, however, thinking "this kingdom is mine", treats (the kingdom) won by force as he pleases, without restraint.
notes: bala-āvarjitam 'won over by force' agrees with the understood kingdom (object of carati, 'deals with'). bala-āvarjitam could also belong inside the quoted thought ('this kingdom won by force is mine'); the translation follows the edition's quotation marks.
lines_deva: नवस् तु राजा बल.आवर्जितं "मम-इदं राज्यम्" इति यथा.इष्टम् अनवग्रहश् चरति
lines_iast: navas tu rājā bala.āvarjitaṃ "mama-idaṃ rājyam" iti yathā.iṣṭam anavagrahaś carati

words.gloss: by those who rose up with him

hindi: अथवा अपने साथ उठ खड़े होने वाले साथियों के द्वारा नियन्त्रित होकर वह राज्य की हानि को सह लेता है।
english: Or, held in check by those who rose up with him, he tolerates injury to the kingdom.
notes: sāmutthāyika = associate in the uprising that brought him to power.
lines_deva: सामुत्थायिकैर् अवगृहीतो वा राज्य.उपघातं मर्षयति

hindi: प्रकृतियों में जड़ न जमाए हुए होने से उसे सरलता से उखाड़ा जा सकता है।
english: Not rooted among the constituent elements, he is easy to uproot.
lines_deva: प्रकृतिष्व् अरूढः सुखम् उच्छेत्तुं भवति-इति

words.gloss: in the case of the sick one

hindi: रोगी राजा के विषय में यह भेद है: एक पापरोग से ग्रस्त और दूसरा पापरोग से ग्रस्त न होने वाला।
english: In the case of the sick one there is a distinction: one with a malignant disease and one without a malignant disease.
notes: The printed pāparogyapāparogī is the sandhi of pāpa-rogī + apāpa-rogī (ī + a > ya); the e-text's dots 'rogya.pāpa' misanalyse the compound boundary but the letters are correct, so no text_flag. pāpa-roga = a grave (incurable or disgraceful) disease.
lines_deva: व्याधिते विशेषः पाप.रोग्य.पाप.रोगी च

words.gloss: in the case of the new one

hindi: नए राजा के विषय में भी भेद है: कुलीन और अकुलीन।
english: In the case of the new one too: well-born and not well-born.
lines_deva: नवे ऽप्य् अभिजातो ऽनभिजात इति

hindi: "दुर्बल कुलीन राजा अथवा बलवान् अकुलीन राजा" — इस विषय में "दुर्बल कुलीन राजा के उपजाप को प्रकृतियाँ उसकी दुर्बलता को देखते हुए कठिनाई से स्वीकार करती हैं, और बलवान् अकुलीन राजा के उपजाप को उसके बल को देखते हुए सरलता से" — ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: "A weak king of high birth or a strong king of low birth": "The constituent elements, having regard to weakness, go along with the secret instigation (upajāpa) of a weak king of high birth only with difficulty, but easily with that of a strong king of low birth, having regard to strength," say the teachers.
notes: upajāpa = secret instigation / overtures. The genitive is ambiguous: instigation made by the king (his overtures to win the subjects), or instigation directed against him by an enemy; translated literally as 'of'. Unit 24's visaṃvādayanti favours the first.
lines_deva: दुर्बलो ऽभिजातो बलवान् अनभिजातो राजा-इति "दुर्बलस्य-अभिजातस्य-उपजापं दौर्बल्य.अपेक्षाः प्रकृतयः कृच्छ्रेण-उपगच्छन्ति, बलवतश् च-अनभिजातस्य बल.अपेक्षाः सुखेन" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: durbalo 'bhijāto balavān anabhijāto rājā-iti "durbalasya-abhijātasya-upajāpaṃ daurbalya.apekṣāḥ prakṛtayaḥ kṛcchreṇa-upagacchanti, balavataś ca-anabhijātasya bala.apekṣāḥ sukhena" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: नहीं, ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: "No," says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः

hindi: दुर्बल कुलीन राजा के अधीन प्रकृतियाँ स्वयं हो जाती हैं; ऐश्वर्य की प्रकृति कुलीन का अनुसरण करती है।
english: The constituent elements of their own accord submit to a weak king of high birth; sovereignty by its nature follows the well-born one.
notes: aiśvarya-prakṛti taken as 'the nature (svabhāva) of sovereignty', i.e. sovereignty by its nature attaches to high birth; the alternative 'the constituents (subjects) of the realm' is possible but aiśvarya is not one of the seven prakṛtis. Hindi प्रकृति covers both senses.
lines_deva: दुर्बलम् अभिजातं प्रकृतयः स्वयम् उपनमन्ति, जात्यम् ऐश्वर्य.प्रकृतिर् अनुवर्तत इति
lines_iast: durbalam abhijātaṃ prakṛtayaḥ svayam upanamanti, jātyam aiśvarya.prakṛtir anuvartata iti

hindi: और बलवान् अकुलीन राजा के उपजाप को वे विफल कर देती हैं; अनुराग में सब गुणों की पूर्णता है।
english: And they frustrate the secret instigation of a strong king of low birth; in affection lies the totality of all qualities.
notes: visaṃvādayanti 'make false, disappoint': the subjects do not respond to his overtures. anurāga = the subjects' affection for the king.
lines_deva: बलवतश् च-अनभिजातस्य-उपजापं विसंवादयन्ति, अनुरागे सार्वगुण्यम् इति
lines_iast: balavataś ca-anabhijātasya-upajāpaṃ visaṃvādayanti, anurāge sārvaguṇyam iti

words.gloss: because of the destruction of effort

hindi: परिश्रम के नष्ट हो जाने के कारण फसल का नाश मुट्ठी-भर अन्न के नाश से अधिक अनिष्टकारी है; जीविका न रह जाने के कारण अनावृष्टि अतिवृष्टि से अधिक अनिष्टकारी है।
english: Because it destroys the effort (spent on it), destruction of the crop is worse than destruction of the handful; because it leaves no livelihood, drought is worse than excessive rain.
notes: Construed on the pattern of the second half: causal ablative + ablative of comparison. Alternative: 'destruction of the crop is worse than destruction of effort (sowing) and than destruction of the handful'. muṣṭi 'handful' is taken as the reaped grain in hand; it could also mean the seed sown. The two halves are two separate comparisons (crops vs. rain). Reviewer: muṣṭi may rather be the handful of seed-grain sown, which suits the 'loss of effort' reason better than reaped grain; translation kept literal ('the handful').
lines_deva: प्रयास.वधात् सस्य.वधो मुष्टि.वधात् पापीयान्, निराजीवत्वाद् अवृष्टिर् अतिवृष्टितः
lines_iast: prayāsa.vadhāt sasya.vadho muṣṭi.vadhāt pāpīyān, nirājīvatvād avṛṣṭir ativṛṣṭitaḥ

hindi: दो-दो व्यसनों के विषय में प्रकृतियों का बल और अबल क्रम-परम्परा से कहा गया है; वही अभियान करने और स्थिर रहने का कारण है।
english: For each pair of calamities, the strength and weakness of the constituent elements has been stated in order of succession; it is the reason for marching and for staying.
notes: Closing verse (anuṣṭubh, 16 syllables a line). dvayor dvayoḥ (repeated) = 'of each two', i.e. of each pair of calamities compared in the chapter. yāne sthāne ca: whether to march (against an enemy in calamity) or to stay.
lines_deva: द्वयोर् द्वयोर् व्यसनयोः प्रकृतीनां बल.अबलम्
पारम्पर्य.क्रमेण-उक्तं याने स्थाने च कारणम्
